chapter_title: Chương 238: 0240 [Vừa đủ điểm chuẩn, có thể đăng ký ngành top đầu cả nước?]

segments.title: Chương 238: 0240 [Vừa đủ điểm chuẩn, có thể đăng ký ngành top đầu cả nước?]
segments.content:
Capital Airport.

Chen Guiliang said to Tao Xue, "This is the first year Sichuan is setting its own exam questions. The Gaokao scores are probably going to be chaotic, and the situation with filling out applications will be even more so. Don't feel bad no matter what you score, and don't be so indecisive when choosing your universities."

"Mm, I know." Tao Xue nodded.

During Chen Guiliang's final exam period, besides traveling around, Tao Xue also visited eight universities with her parents.

They were all ones with admission scores that roughly matched her level.

Once Chen Guiliang's finals were over, it was about time for Tao Xue to go back, check her score, and fill out her application.

Chen Guiliang had heard a little about this year's Sichuan Gaokao in his past life, but he wasn't particularly clear on the specific details.

The general situation seemed to be that test-takers from Chengdu and Mianzhou crowded the province's high-score brackets. The other cities, on the other hand, collectively bombed the exam, with Longdu City being among the worst.

But at the time, no one understood the full picture.

The high-scoring students in Chengdu and Mianzhou, seeing so many high-scorers around them, got scared and were extremely conservative when filling out their applications.

Meanwhile, students from the other cities collectively fell into a state of confusion.

There were even some who had just barely passed the cutoff score for famous universities, who under normal circumstances would have a zero percent chance of getting in. But some students, with nothing to lose, not only applied to top universities but also intentionally chose popular majors and checked "do not accept major reallocation." After submitting their applications, they went straight home to prepare for another year of review, planning to retake the exam, only to be accepted into a good major at a top university in a completely absurd turn of events.

It was the first time the province was setting its own exam questions. From teachers to students, no one had any experience, so everyone could only fill out their applications blindly.

Tao Xue returned to her hometown. At 10 p.m. the next evening, she could check her score on her phone.

After checking, Tao Xue was completely dumbfounded.

Her parents could only try to console her, but it was no use. Frightened, they kept urging her not to do anything foolish.

The next day, she went to school.

Tao Xue had been in a regular class in her first year of high school. When classes were split into liberal arts and sciences in the second year, she was selected for the liberal arts experimental class based on her first-year final exam results.

Her head teacher was a woman in her forties. She announced with a smile, "The city's top scorer in liberal arts is in our class. Congratulations to student Li Qian..."

After a round of celebration, the head teacher called the city's top liberal arts scorer, Li Qian, out to the hallway alone. "I called a friend to ask. There are a ton of high-scorers in Chengdu and Mianzhou. Also, the situation this year is very strange. Peking University's cutoff score for liberal arts is only 4 points higher than Tsinghua's. That's never happened before. I can't give you any advice. You'll have to decide for yourself."

Li Qian's Gaokao score was more than 10 points higher than the cutoff for Peking and Tsinghua Universities.

But in Chengdu and Mianzhou alone, the number of students with scores higher than hers was greater than the total number of admission slots Peking and Tsinghua had for all of Sichuan.

The city's top liberal arts scorer, after much thought and repeated consideration, applied to Renmin University when she filled out her application.

When Tao Xue heard the news, her emotional breakdown worsened.

She called Chen Guiliang to vent her grievances. "Senior, I did badly on my exam."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Don't panic. Tell me what happened."

Tao Xue said, "In my three mock exams, my score was about 30 points higher than the Tier 1 university cutoff line. This time, I'm only 6 points over the Tier 1 line. It's such an awkward score. If I apply to a Tier 1 university, it'll be hard to get into my first choice."

"Accept major reallocation then," Chen Guiliang suggested.

Given the situation in Sichuan this year, even Zhang Xuefeng would be at a loss, because filling out the applications was a state of pure chaos. The students were all applying blindly, which greatly affected each school's admissions.

Tao Xue said, "The liberal arts and science streams at No. 2 High both bombed this year. The city's top liberal arts scorer is in my class. I just asked her which school she applied to, and she actually said she applied to Renmin University."

"What an unlucky kid," Chen Guiliang remarked with a sigh.

Tao Xue said, "I'll look into it some more."

She hung up the phone and stared at the reference book the school had handed out.

Tao Chenggang learned of the situation from her parents and invited an "expert" to help her figure it out.

The "expert" was also a bit baffled this year, because through his extensive connections, he had gathered a lot of information. But the more he knew, the more his brain couldn't keep up.

"Do you have any requirements for your major?" the expert asked.

Tao Xue said, "No requirements, just the closer to Peking University, the better."

The expert advised, "For your first choice, apply to Minzu University of China for Ethnology. It's the school's ace major, number one in the country. But it's very unpopular, and there aren't enough applicants from Sichuan every year. Your score should be enough to get in."

This was a very strange way of finding a loophole.

In 2006, judging by the ethnology major alone, Minzu University of China was first, Caiyun Nationalities University was second, and Peking University could only rank third.

But for this number-one major in the country, not many students in Sichuan province applied. There were even absurd cases where students applied for a useless but popular major and ended up being reallocated to this ace major.

He didn't know about other provinces, but this had indeed been the case in Sichuan for the past few years.

Of course, as information became more accessible, the actual admission score for this major at Minzu University of China would get higher and higher in the future.

"Huh?"

Tao Xue had no concept of ethnology. She asked, "Can I apply for journalism or Chinese language? I'm slightly interested in those two."

The expert said, "If it's for journalism or Chinese language at Minzu University of China, it'll be very difficult for you to get in with your score. You can apply, but you'll have to accept major reallocation. You might be reassigned to some random major, so you'd be better off just applying directly for the ace major, ethnology."

Tao Xue asked again, "What about other schools?"

The expert said, "Normally, I could give you a lot of suggestions, but you require it to be close to Peking University. There's also China University of Petroleum. Majors like English, economics, public administration, business administration, political theory... these are all relatively safe bets. But the university's focus is different. For example, their English program emphasizes energy trade. Their political theory program emphasizes party-building in oil fields."

The expert went on to mention a few more schools and, based on Tao Xue's wishes, gave her a complete application plan.

Her first choice was Minzu University of China, which was not only very close to Peking University but even closer to Renmin University. She could even visit Renmin University in her spare time and hang out with this year's unlucky city top scorer.

And, Tao Xue really did apply directly for ethnology!

Even though she had no idea what you even did with it after studying it.

But Tao Xue still harbored some fantasies. She had recently been reading *Ghost Blows Out the Light* and was thinking about how she could study those legendary peoples in the future.

The Jingjue Kingdom seemed to belong to the Ghost-Cave Tribe. Did this tribe actually exist in history, or did the author just make it up?

Tao Xue called Chen Guiliang and said, "Haha, when I graduate, I'm going to be an explorer, specializing in the study of those vanished peoples and civilizations."

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "You've been reading too much *Ghost Blows Out the Light*. Don't mistake a novel for reality."

"I don't care, I've already submitted my application," Tao Xue said, then complained again, "What the hell is with the Gaokao this year? I heard from the expert that the whole province is in chaos right now. No matter if you have a high score or a low score, nobody knows how to fill out their application."

Sigh, one could only say that Tao Xue was unlucky to be a guinea pig for the province's first independently administered exam.

Beijing.

Yang Shuo was driving, with Chen Guiliang and Bian Guanyue sitting in the back.

Bian Guanyue was about to leave Beijing after her exams. She had to go back to Sichuan for the summer break to continue her studies with an old folk artist.

Over the past year or so, she had become obsessed with it.

"Which school did Tao Xue apply to?" Bian Guanyue asked.

Chen Guiliang said, "Minzu University, a little south of Renmin University. And for ethnology, of all things. I find it hard to imagine her applying for that major."

Bian Guanyue thought to herself: *She really followed him all the way to Beijing. Ugh, so annoying!*

Chen Guiliang made a few more calls and eventually managed to ask an ethnology student at Peking University.

The student was speechless when he heard the story. "What's the situation? Someone from Sichuan can get into Minzu University's ethnology program with a score just a few points over the Tier 1 line? What the hell, then what was the point of me getting a super high score to get into Peking University, only to be reallocated to ethnology? Her major is ranked even higher than ours at Peking University!"

This was, of course, just a silly complaint. The two schools had different focuses; Peking University's ethnology program was more global in scope.

After talking for a while, Chen Guiliang hung up the phone.
